final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the claim by reframing the same record. That reframing is more careful than the original certification claim, but it still does not cure the core compliance gap. The admissible evidence supports that aggregate readiness clears threshold and that rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents. It also supports that the enterprise refund workflow misses target, is named in a renewal success plan, legal has not closed review, and policy requires disclosure or approved risk acceptance for material limitations affecting named launch use cases. That means the record may support a bounded technical-readiness argument, but it does not support present policy closure. This is not enough for compliant_with_caveats because the caveat is itself an unresolved compliance predicate, not merely a residual operational risk to monitor.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows completed disclosure for the material limitation before launch.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering the limitation before launch.
Legal review remains open, so the policy predicate is unresolved on the present record.
The affected enterprise refund workflow is tied to a named customer commitment, which sustains materiality under the policy text.
Public governance guidance on documentation and monitoring does not satisfy the internal disclosure-or-acceptance requirement.
